<reason>B wins on the surviving exemption-or-defiance dilemma: either genuine shortage is exempt and the rule changes nothing, or it is not and enforcement requires unverifiable surplus judgments and famine-time penalties that punish workers and foreign-exchange earnings. B also showed reserves and financing are not created by limiting bans, while A increasingly relied on added observatory, sanctions, and insurance machinery and suffered a clipped closing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Rebuttal 2 answer that a ban is a brake on private traders, so removing it compels outflows even without an affordable surplus, directly neutralized A's strongest pressure question and crystallized the verification trap.</best_rebuttal>
